content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], [user_name], [user_name], and [user_name], I have a kilowatt/power transducer with an output of 4 to 20 mA. - 4 mA = -1250 kW - 12 mA = 0 kW - 20 mA = +1250 kW My questions are: 1) How should I wire the -VE connection between the analog module and the kilowatt transducer? 2) When using the analog threshold trigger function, for example: Trigger ON from -1250 kW to +250 kW or +350 kW. Trigger OFF from +250 kW or +350 kW up to +1250 kW. What values should be set for the trigger ON and OFF in this scenario? Looking forward to your responses. Thanks, and merry Christmas to everyone. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, If you think through the problem a little further, you'll find an easy solution: Use an analog amplifier for the 4–20 mA sensor (range: min: -1250, max: 1250), followed by setting an analog threshold trigger. For settings: ON at 0, OFF at 250 (or 350). Good luck.

Hi, thank you for your reply. My questions are: 1) How do I correctly wire the -VE between the analog module and the kilowatt transducer? 2) When using the analog threshold trigger function: - Trigger ON from -1250 to 250 kW or 350 kW. - Trigger OFF from 250 kW or 350 kW up to +1250 kW. What settings should be used for the analog threshold values for trigger ON and OFF in this example? I look forward to your responses. Best regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discussed how to set up an analog module to process a 4–20 mA signal from a power transducer, focusing on calculating proper threshold values for triggering logic functions. There was some initial confusion regarding wiring and threshold settings, but users exchanged solutions and calculation files to assist each other.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek clear guidance on wiring the analog module with a power transducer and accurate information on configuring threshold values for logic implementation using the hardware.
